definitions.fact_key: per update, over every model's and repeat's accepted facts: the connected components of the bench's agreement heuristic (scripts/bench_tf_handover.py reference_match: same type, and one quote contains the other after episode.norm); a key is named by its type and its shortest normalized quote; a repeat's fact set is the set of keys of its accepted facts (two facts of one repeat in one key count once)
definitions.used_pairs: a (model, update) pair is used when every repeat of it completed (status ok)
definitions.within_model_jaccard: per (model, update): the mean Jaccard over the 3 pairs of repeat fact sets; per model: the mean over updates; Jaccard of two empty sets is 1
definitions.repeat_count: in how many of a model's repeats of an update the key was accepted (1..repeats)
definitions.majority_vote_set: the keys a model accepted in more than half of its repeats of an update (2 of 3)
definitions.cross_model_jaccard: per update: Jaccard of the two models' majority-vote sets; mean over updates
definitions.other_model_present: the other model accepted the same key in at least one of its repeats of the update
definitions.reference_match: at least one of this model's accepted facts in the key has the type of a fact of the story's recorded extraction for that update and one quote contains the other (reference_match); the reference is the story's recorded extraction (the fixture's curated facts for each update), matched with the bench's heuristic (same type, one quote contains the other); it is not clinical ground truth and not a quality score
definitions.unit_of_the_rates: one (model, update, key); 'pooled' adds both models' units
definitions.proposal_key: 3(a) only: as fact_key, but over every proposal of the update (accepted_facts and rejected_facts of the completed case records); a proposal without a text quote or type keys by what it has, so such proposals of one type share a key; sections 1, 2 and 3(b) keep the accepted-fact keys
definitions.grounding_repeat_count: 3(a): in how many of a model's repeats of an update the proposal key was proposed (accepted or rejected)
definitions.grounding_other_model_present: 3(a): the other model proposed the same proposal key in at least one of its repeats of the update
definitions.grounding_accepted: 3(a), unit (model, update, proposal key): every one of this model's proposals in the key passed the grounding check (episode.grounding_problem); the proposal rows count each proposal instead (accepted proposals / proposals)
definitions.bootstrap: percentile 2.5 / 97.5 of the mean over 2000 resamples of the updates with replacement, seed 20261017 with a per-statistic key (bench_tf_handover.bootstrap_ci), no interval below n = 5

grounding_acceptance.note: a proposal is a fact the model proposed that the grounding check judged (episode.grounding_problem): accepted_facts plus rejected_facts of the case record; facts the evidence gate withheld are in neither

caveats: The reference is the story's recorded extraction (the demo fixture's curated facts), matched by the bench's heuristic (same type, one quote contains the other). It is not clinical ground truth and not a quality score: a correct fact the fixture does not list, or one the model typed differently, counts as unmatched.

n is small: 12 updates of one fictional story, 3 repeats, 2 models. The bootstrap resamples updates; the Wilson intervals treat each (model, update, key) as independent, which keys of one update or of both models are not, so the intervals are optimistic.

Grounding-check acceptance (3a) uses proposal keys, built like the fact keys over accepted and rejected proposals together, so they can differ from the accepted-fact keys of sections 1, 2 and 3(b) (a rejected proposal can join two accepted keys or stand alone). The check is deterministic: a proposal repeated word for word gets the same verdict, so a key's repeat count measures how often the model re-proposed it, not independent re-checks. A key counts as accepted only when all of the model's proposals in it passed, so a key proposed in more repeats has more chances to fail; the proposal column counts each proposal, which treats repeats of one proposal as independent and is more optimistic still.

Keys come from quote containment, chained through a group: 15 key(s) group several distinct quotes and 3 are bridged (two quotes joined only through a third, e.g. two half-sentence facts and one whole-sentence fact). A model that splits a sentence into two facts in one repeat and quotes it whole in another counts as stable; facts of different types never share a key.
A key's reference match counts any of the model's member quotes, so a key seen in more repeats has slightly more chances to match.

The other-model split and the reference match use the same test (same type, one quote contains the other), so a fact given an unusual type fails both: part of that split measures agreement on the type label, not only on the content.
Repeat variation is what the endpoint returned under the bench's settings (see its results.json); the analysis does not know the sampling parameters.
